A Playwright trace corpus of the INS frontend's fit specs, recorded at trade-imports-ins-frontend 406e300: 50 folders under workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/traces-ins-fit/, each holding one trace.zip, plus report.json (the Playwright JSON report, with an npm/webpack preamble before the JSON) that maps every test to its folder. All 50 tests passed. They come from 7 spec files: fit/smoke.fit.spec.js (1 test: sign in, dashboard, add, view and delete an address), and under src/server/app/features/: address-book/fit/add.fit.spec.js (21 tests: the add form, 7 empty-field errors, 8 over-length errors, a malformed email, two axe checks, save and cancel), address-book/fit/list.fit.spec.js (6: navigation, the table, add link, axe, pagination over 25, empty state), address-book/fit/view.fit.spec.js (5: open, every Standard Address Block field, Edit and Delete, Back, axe), address-book/fit/edit.fit.spec.js (7: prefill, axe, rejected save keeps edits, malformed email, error-state axe, save, cancel) and address-book/fit/delete.fit.spec.js (4: confirmation, cancel, confirm, axe), and dashboard/dashboard.fit.spec.js (6: statuses and columns, axe, submitted links to notification-view, draft links to the journey hub, search by reference, no results). It covers the INS front door only: the address book (list, view, add, edit, delete) and the notifications dashboard, as the real INS frontend renders them today. It leaves out the animals journey, which trace:animals-fit holds. The corpus is indexed from report.json in trace-ins-fit.work/index.md. The traces were written by Playwright 1.63.0 and tim's bundled Playwright (1.62.1) cannot open them (TraceVersionError), so action and error counts are not indexed, and each part also names its spec file so the agent can read the steps and asserted copy until tim's Playwright is upgraded.

Extracted in 4 parts:
Part 1, address-book/fit/add.fit.spec.js: Part 1 mined all 21 traces of repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend/src/server/app/features/address-book/fit/add.fit.spec.js (spec read in full, with its helper address-form.js for the labels and messages the tests drive). The Playwright CLI that tim runs refused these zips (TraceVersionError: trace created by a newer Playwright), so each trace was read from its already-unpacked copy in this part's work folder (render, axe, req-name, req-line1, req-town, req-postcode, req-country, req-phone, req-email, max-name, max-line1, max-line2, max-town, max-county, max-postcode, max-phone, max-email, bad-email, err-axe, save, cancel): actions from 1-trace.trace 'before' events, the network log from 1-trace.network, and every frame snapshot rendered to HTML with a jq filter (render.jq), plus test.trace for the axe results. Refs below name the trace by its folder hash (for example a-31686) and the action's callId. Pages, in order: (1) stub sign-in GET /auth/stub-sign-in?organisationId=... which 302s to / ('Dashboard | Import notification service'), always, as the harness entry; (2) the add address page GET /address-book/add, 'Add address details', always: two H2 sections ('Enter address details': Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country select; 'Enter contact details': Email address, Phone number with hint), then 'Save and continue' and 'Cancel and return to address book' buttons; (3) the same page in its error state, conditional on a failed submit (POST returns 400, title prefixed 'Error: ', error summary 'There is a problem' with one link per error, inline error message, value preserved): driven for 7 empty required fields, 8 over-length fields and 1 malformed email, one error per trace; (4) the address book list GET /address-book after a successful save (POST 302) with the 'Success' notification banner and the new row, or after cancel (POST 302, no banner, nothing created). Two traces ran axe on page 2 and page 3: both reported zero serious or critical violations. The add page and its error state are built entirely from govuk-frontend components (Input, Select, Hint, Error summary, Error message, Button, secondary Button, Button group); no non-govuk class appears inside main. No caption and no back link render on the add page. The country list held only 4 countries. No backend call is visible: the frontend's calls to the address book service are server side and leave no trace in the browser network log.
Part 2, address-book list and view: Part 2, address-book list and view. Read in full: list.fit.spec.js and view.fit.spec.js, and all 11 traces they recorded (list.fit 762a7 navigation, 3e618 table, fe734 add link, 49f4e axe, d7e93 pagination, 964e2 empty state; view.fit 4a433 open from a row, cd84f every field, 2e5d8 Edit and Delete, 4811a Back, 14089 axe). tim's bundled Playwright cannot open these traces (TraceVersionError), so each trace's unzipped contents in this part's working folder were read directly: test.trace for the action list (every action transcribed) and 1-trace.trace for the DOM snapshots, rendered to HTML with jq, plus 1-trace.network for the requests. Pages reached, in order: stub sign-in (302) lands on the Dashboard at / (part 4 owns its content; only the service navigation is claimed here); the Address book list at /address-book (title 'Address book | Import notification service', H1 'Address book', intro line, a Search addresses form, an Add a new address button-link, a 'Showing x-y of z' results label, a table of Name, Address, Country and a visually hidden Action column with a View link per row); the same list at /address-book?page=2 when an organisation has 30 addresses (25 per page, GOV.UK pagination with numbered links, Next and Previous); the empty state for an organisation with no addresses (message, no table, no results label, the Add a new address button still shown); the view address page at /address-book/{id} (title and H1 are the address name, a Back link to /address-book above main, a summary list of nine Standard Address Block rows, then Edit and Delete button-links in a button group). The Add a new address click is followed only as far as the add form's URL and heading; parts 1 and 3 own the add, edit and delete pages. Both pages are entirely govuk-frontend components (service navigation, table, pagination, button, summary list, back link, input, button group). Each page passed an axe check for serious or critical violations. All page loads are server-rendered GETs; no address-book API call is visible from the browser, so the backend integration is recorded as a gap. Search, an unknown address id, ordering rules and pagination beyond two pages were never exercised and are recorded as gaps.
Part 3, address-book edit and delete: Part 3, address-book edit and delete. Read in full: edit.fit.spec.js (7 tests) and delete.fit.spec.js (4 tests) in trade-imports-ins-frontend, plus axe.js for the axe tags, and all 11 trace zips the part names. The tim trace CLI refused every zip (TraceVersionError: trace created by a newer Playwright than tim's viewer), so each trace was mined from its unzipped raw files in this part's work folder (edit-prefill 759a1, edit-axe dafdd, edit-rejected af334, edit-email e9676, edit-erraxe dd003, edit-save de4e5, edit-cancel 36446, del-confirm 967cd, del-cancel d5c0d, del-yes fe6bc, del-axe 7d4d4): the test.trace step list (every navigate, fill, click and expect with its locator), the 1-trace.network log (method, URL, status, Location, form body) and the rendered HTML resources. Action ids in refs are the test.trace callIds (pw:api@N, expect@N). Pages, in order: (1) Edit address details, /address-book/{id}/edit, always reached by direct navigation after stub sign-in; its validation error state (HTTP 400 re-render, same URL), driven by an empty name and by a malformed email; save (302 to /address-book with a success banner) and Cancel (302 to /address-book, nothing saved). (2) Delete address, /address-book/{id}/delete, a confirmation with a warning button and Cancel; Cancel 302s to the details page /address-book/{id}, confirming 302s to /address-book with a success banner and, for the only address, the empty state. The address book list and details pages appear only as landing pages; part 2 owns them. Every surface is entirely govuk-* inside main. Axe runs on the edit page, its error state and the delete page, each with no violations of any impact. Gaps recorded: other edit validation messages, unknown or foreign ids, downstream failure, the entry controls, editing country and optional fields, and the effect of deleting an address in use.
Part 4, dashboard and smoke: Part 4, dashboard and smoke. Read in full: dashboard/dashboard.fit.spec.js (6 tests) and fit/smoke.fit.spec.js (1 test), and all 7 trace zips the part names. tim's Playwright (1.62.1) refuses these traces (TraceVersionError, confirmed again on this run), so each trace was read from its unzipped contents in this part's working folder (t1..t7), with jq over the browser trace (1-trace.trace: every call, every frame snapshot), the network log (1-trace.network) and the test step log (test.trace). Trace map: t1 = dashboard-dashboard.fit-da-7c8cd (spec :23, AC1/AC2 statuses and columns), t2 = da-62c16 (spec :54, axe), t3 = da-44f5e (spec :61, submitted link to notification-view), t4 = da-2eeb5 (spec :74, draft link to journey hub), t5 = da-21d7c (spec :87, search by reference), t6 = da-7e579 (spec :106, No notifications found), t7 = smoke.fit-a-trader-signs-i-62e11 (smoke.fit.spec.js:13). Pages, in journey order: stub sign-in (/auth/stub-sign-in?organisationId=..., a 302 with no page of its own) -> Dashboard (/, title 'Dashboard | Import notification service') in three states: the default list (t1-t4, t7, call@259/call@13), search results (t5 call@295, ?sort=arrivalDate%2Cdesc&referenceNumber=GBN-AG-26-000001) and no results (t6 call@265, referenceNumber=GBN-AG-26-999999). The smoke trace then walks the address book: list (/address-book) -> add (/address-book/add) -> list with success banner -> view (/address-book/<id>) -> delete (/address-book/<id>/delete) -> list with deleted banner, then axe; those pages are claimed here only as the signed-in journey, since parts 1 to 3 own their detail. The dashboard itself is always present after sign-in; the search-results and no-results states appear only after a search.
